purpose: Qualify current public DOC repeated-edit latency and allocation/peak-live scaling under existing bounded render-retention controls; same-build route comparison, no production optimization or new adoption claim.
operation: Fresh public snapshot/edit; repeat replace_paragraph(Position(0)) alternating the retained0730 FIRST_TEXT and SECOND_TEXT; commit and materialize output. Same-object repeated edits, not bulk distinct-paragraph editing.

native.case_and_edit_order: odd numbered rounds use fixture and edit order above; even rounds reverse both
native.timer: Complete public in-memory lifecycle, including input clone/open, edit construction, all mutations, optional release, commit, output copy and local owner destruction. File I/O, preparation, correctness checks and JSON serialization excluded. No per-stage timing or diagnostic callbacks.

allocator.schedule: repetition1 fixtures/edits/routes in listed order; repetition2 reverse all three
allocator.scope: Separate System allocator instrumented binary; region starts before input clone/open and ends with only output allocation retained. Stage observations use fixed stack storage. Report requested allocated/deallocated bytes, successful allocation calls, relative peak-live and retained bytes. No instrumented latency claim.

bootstrap.unit: matched round within fixed fixture/edit count
bootstrap.statistic: median of per-round zero-p50/route-p50 ratios for default and release

review_flags.meaning: Report flags per fixture/count/route; flags are review triggers, not sample exclusion or adoption gates. Allocation repeat differences remain visible.

mandatory_gates: all requested stages are distinct changes
forward patch equality and exact inverse source restoration
stale or foreign source refusals as defined by current API
untouched stream bytes and directory metadata preservation
zero route retains no render and release route clears every stage
allocator retained bytes match only output allocation capacity
source and fixture files unchanged through build and capture
capture_rules: Freeze exact source/build/binary/probe/runner identities before measured children.
Functional qualification before capture is separate and not part of performance statistics.
No overwriting, selective reruns, dropped samples or adverse-row replacement.
Root starts native schedule only after coordinated profiling/build/quality work is idle; unrelated shared-host activity is uncontrolled.
Record command/environment, start/end times, exit status and host load for each child.
Separate native clocks, allocation region metrics and whole-child RSS.
All files >=1MiB and all compiled executables stay outside Git; retain reduced descriptors and regeneration commands.
